title: Nasu — 那須
goal: Describe length and quantity without confusing adjectives with modifiers.

blocks.text: Nasu is a highland area in northern Tochigi, associated with outdoor scenery and hot springs. The app's fixed **Nasu** location is retained; a lesson location does not have to be a legally incorporated city.
**那須の山を見ます。** なすの やまを みます。 — I look at the mountains in Nasu.
Our road lengths, crowds and food quantities are imaginary. We make descriptions of a scene; we do not supply a real hiking distance, crowd forecast or medical claim about bathing.

items: **Character:** 那 · **Meaning/reading orientation:** な in this name · **Radical/components:** 邑 as right 阝, おおざと; left is a changed sound-related shape, not 月 · **Status:** Assisted encounter.

**Character:** 須 · **Meaning/reading orientation:** requirement/beard orientation; す here · **Radical/components:** 頁, おおがい, with 彡 on the left · **Status:** Assisted encounter; three slants are 彡, not 川.

blocks.text: **那須 / なす**. 須's beard-related historical formation should not be converted into a modern “bearded town” story. The ordinary vegetable **なす**, eggplant, shares the sound but is a different word; its harder kanji are not required here.
**長い / ながい — long.** 長 is its own radical, ながい; learn its long vertical and lower sweeping strokes as one complex whole form. It is not just an elongated 木.
**この道は長いです。** このみちは ながいです。 — This road is long.

**長い道 / ながいみち — a long road.** Like familiar 高い, this is an ordinary い-adjective: **長くないです / ながくないです**, not long; **長かったです / ながかったです**, was long; **長くなかったです / ながくなかったです**, was not long. We describe length, not automatically travel time.
**短い / みじかい — short.** 短 has radical 矢, やへん, beside 豆, a sound-related component. The left has an arrow-shaped form, not 牛. Its shape helps distinguish it from 長.
**この道は短いです。** このみちは みじかいです。 — This road is short.
**短い文を読みます。** みじかい ぶんを よみます。 — I read a short sentence.
Both roads and text can have length. **短かったです / みじかかったです** is the past description. Do not confuse **小さい**, small in size, with **短い**, short in length, though English contexts can sometimes overlap.

**多い / おおい — many/a lot; たくさん — many/a lot**, useful quantity word. 多 has radical 夕, ゆうべ; recognise the two similar 夕 forms. These are indexing/shape facts, not a claim that quantity means “two evenings.”
**人が多いです。** ひとが おおいです。 — There are many people.
**たくさんの人がいます。** たくさんの ひとが います。 — There are many people.
The course uses 多い as a predicate and **たくさんの人** before a noun. Avoid the beginner error **多い人** for “many people”; Japanese quantity phrasing differs from ordinary length adjectives.

cards.title: 少: few; 少し: a little

blocks.text: **少ない / すくない — few/little; 少し / すこし — a little.** 少 has radical 小, しょう; notice the extra slanting stroke that distinguishes 少 from 小. The two words share a character but have different grammar roles.
**人が少ないです。** ひとが すくないです。 — There are few people.
**水を少し飲みます。** みずを すこし のみます。 — I drink a little water.
少ない describes quantity; 少し can modify the amount of an action. **少ない人** is not our basic phrase for “few people.” Use 人が少ないです in this beginner pattern.

items: **Meaning:** many · **Present:** 多い / おおい · **Negative:** 多くない / おおくない · **Past:** 多かった / おおかった · **Past negative:** 多くなかった / おおくなかった
**Meaning:** few · **Present:** 少ない / すくない · **Negative:** 少なくない / すくなくない · **Past:** 少なかった / すくなかった · **Past negative:** 少なくなかった / すくなくなかった

blocks.text: Add です for our polite descriptions. **人が多くなかったです。** ひとが おおくなかったです。 — There were not many people. **少なくない** literally means not few; it need not mean exactly the same quantity as 多い. Negation does not supply an exact count.

cards.title: Quantity does not give a number

blocks.text: **人が多いです。** ひとが おおいです。 — There are many people.
**人が五人います。** ひとが ごにん います。 — There are five people.

The first is relative to a context or expectation. The second provides an exact count. You cannot infer five from 多い alone. Likewise 長い says something is long; without a measurement it does not mean a fixed number of kilometres or minutes. Scored questions keep those two kinds of evidence separate.

cards.title: Compare scenes without new comparison grammar

blocks.text: **この道は長いです。その道は短いです。** このみちは ながいです。そのみちは みじかいです。 — This road is long. That road is short.
**朝は人が少ないです。昼は人が多いです。** あさは ひとが すくないです。ひるは ひとが おおいです。 — In the morning there are few people. At midday there are many.
These are descriptions of a fictional day. They do not yet teach より/ほうが comparison grammar or claim actual Nasu crowd patterns.
**A: この道は長いですか。** このみちは ながいですか。 — Is this road long?
**B: はい、長いです。** はい、ながいです。 — Yes, it is long.
**A: 少し休みませんか。** すこし やすみませんか。 — Shall we rest a little?
**B: はい、休みましょう。** はい、やすみましょう。 — Yes, let's rest.
少し makes the amount of rest small without giving a precise time. 一時間 would specify an hour. The invitation still comes from the known polite stem rather than a new ability or desire form.

items: Read 那須, 長い, 短い, 多い, 少ない, 少し. **Answers:** なす; ながい; みじかい; おおい; すくない; すこし.
Which radical is in 短? **Answer:** 矢.
Which is our “many people” noun phrase: 多い人 / たくさんの人? **Answer:** たくさんの人.
Make 長いです past negative. **Answer:** 長くなかったです.
Does 多い give an exact count? **Answer:** No.
“Drink a little water”: 水を＿＿飲みます。 **Answer:** 少し.

blocks.text: 那須 is なす; 那 has right 阝/邑 and 須 has 頁 with 彡. 長い/短い describe length. 多い/少ない describe quantity as predicates in our basic models. Use たくさんの人 for the taught noun phrase, and 少し to modify a small amount of an action. These qualitative words do not supply exact measurements.
**Recall:** “There are few people. Let's rest a little.” **Model:** 人が少ないです。少し休みましょう。 ひとが すくないです。すこし やすみましょう。 Complete Tochigi's reading and test before Gunma.
